reasoning: Hard Kelvin gate failure across two cables: cable 1 is symmetric (both /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO unrouted), cable 2 is asymmetric (/SENSEC2_HI unrouted, /SENSEC2_LO apparently routed). However, kelvin_unrouted=1 only counts cable 1's symmetric failure; cable 2's asymmetric failure is invisible to that metric and only surfaces in unconnected=4 (3 Kelvin-related ratlines + 1 non-Kelvin) and the binary gate_fail=1. This creates a scoring blind spot: two candidates where (a) only cable 1 symmetrically fails vs (b) cable 1 symmetrically fails AND cable 2 asymmetrically fails receive identical kelvin_unrouted=1 and gate_fail=1 scores, giving FR zero differentiated scoring pressure to prefer clearing cable 2's half-broken Kelvin pair. The unconnected metric is the only current lever capturing /SENSEC2_HI as a ratline. Additionally, all 7 compiler stubs targeted non-failing nets (/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA) with 100% elimination — the classic double_blindness state where Rules 40/41 should arm next-round absorber bypass. DRC=28 at round 89 indicates either DRC violations are entangled with the Kelvin routing channels or cosmetic/logo DRC is eroding candidate quality; Rule 45 addresses shunt-proximate DRC clearance only on absorber-bypass dispatch, leaving unaddressed the scenario where DRC remains high across many non-bypass rounds and the violations become self-reinforcing with blocked Kelvin paths.

scorer_penalty.rationale: Cable 2's asymmetric Kelvin failure (/SENSEC2_HI unrouted) does not register in kelvin_unrouted because that metric requires both pair members to be unrouted to increment. Its sole scoring pressure comes through the unconnected ratline count. Raising unconnected from 550 to 700 increases the per-ratline penalty for all remaining ratlines — including Kelvin-adjacent ones that asymmetric failure leaves invisible to kelvin_unrouted — improving candidate discrimination when kelvin_unrouted undercounts the true number of cables with active Kelvin issues.

manager_rule: Maintain a session-scoped integer counter 'consecutive_high_drc_kelvin_stall'. After each round R: if structural DRC > 20 AND kelvin_unrouted > 0, increment the counter; otherwise reset it to 0. When the counter reaches 5: (1) query all structural DRC violation loci from round R's DRC output; (2) group loci into spatial clusters where any two loci within 4 mm of each other belong to the same cluster; (3) rank clusters by error count descending; (4) for the top-2 clusters by count: if the cluster centroid falls within 4 mm of the bounding box of any failing Kelvin cable C's /SENSEC{C}_HI and /SENSEC{C}_LO shunt pad centroids (the shunt-proximate test), issue a ripup directive for every track or via at that cluster's loci AND inject a 3 mm keepout covering those loci for the immediately following round; (5) if a top-2 cluster is NOT shunt-proximate for any failing cable, skip the ripup for that cluster to avoid disrupting non-blocking regions; (6) after cluster ripup, proceed with normal stub injection and Rule-33 force-injection for the round; (7) log 'drc_stagnation_cluster_ripup' with fields: (a) round number R, (b) counter value, (c) all cluster centroids and error counts, (d) which clusters were deemed shunt-proximate and for which cable index C, (e) ripup loci issued, (f) keepout geometries injected; (8) reset consecutive_high_drc_kelvin_stall to 0 after this action regardless of whether the Kelvin gate clears that round. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 40-46 and does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, or any session-scoped state maintained by those rules. Distinction from Rule 45: Rule 45 fires immediately before absorber-bypass dispatch rounds when DRC > 20; this rule fires after 5 consecutive stuck rounds regardless of bypass state, addressing the case where DRC and Kelvin failure remain co-elevated across extended non-bypass stretches where Rule 45 has no trigger. Rationale: at round 89, DRC=28 persisting alongside kelvin_unrouted > 0 indicates geometric congestion near the shunt is not resolving through normal FR optimization or bypass-round-only spatial ripup. A threshold-triggered cluster ripup independent of bypass state breaks the mutual reinforcement between residual DRC violations and blocked Kelvin paths by clearing the densest conflict regions before the next routing attempt.
